Based on my search, here's what I found about the Gleam compiler error related to using record update syntax on constructors with no labelled fields:

## The Error

The message "This constructor has no labelled fields" appears when you try to use Gleam's record update syntax (`..`) on a record variant whose fields are not labelled. The analysis of record update expressions is now fault-tolerant, and the compiler now shows a better error message when trying to use the record update syntax with variants that have no labelled fields. This improvement was contributed by Giacomo Cavalieri.

## Why This Happens

Record update syntax relies on labels to know which fields to keep and which to replace. To aid readability Gleam allows fields to be labelled with a name. Labels can be used to give arguments in any order to the constructor of a record.

However, fields don't have to be labelled. You can define a type with positional-only fields:

When a custom type variant holds data it is called a record, and each contained value resides in a field. pub type Rectangle { Rectangle(Float, Float) }

If a constructor's fields have no labels, there's no way to reference individual fields in an update expression—hence the error.

## The Fix

Add labels to your constructor's fields. Instead of positional fields, define them with names:

```gleam
pub type Rectangle {
  Rectangle(
    width: Float,
    height: Float,
  )
}
```

Once labels are present, the record update syntax can be used when a custom type has a single variant to create a new record from an existing one, but with some of the fields replaced with new values.

## Additional Notes

A related restriction is that this type has multiple constructors so it cannot be safely updated. If this value was one of the other variants then the update would produce incorrect results. So record updates work most cleanly on types with a single variant (or after pattern-matching narrows the variant).

In summary: to resolve "This constructor has no labelled fields," add named labels to the fields of the constructor you're trying to update, since the record update syntax fundamentally requires labelled fields to function.

## Summary

The `RecordUpdateInvalidConstructor` error was being used for two distinct situations: (a) something that isn't a record constructor at all (a function, local variable, etc.), and (b) a record constructor that *is* valid but has only positional/unlabelled fields. The task requires the latter to get its own, clearer error message while leaving the former unchanged.

### Source changes

1. **`compiler-core/src/type_/error.rs`** — Added a new `TypeError` variant `RecordUpdateVariantWithNoFields { location }` (with a doc comment) and registered it in the `location`/`start` match arm.

   - Title: `Invalid record constructor`
   - Label: `This constructor has no labelled fields`
   - Text (via `wrap`): `Only constructors with at least one labelled field can be used with the update syntax.`

3. **`compiler-core/src/type_/expression.rs`** — Switched the two `field_map: None` raise sites (the record-update expression path in `infer_record_update_variant`, and the constant record-update path) from `RecordUpdateInvalidConstructor` to `RecordUpdateVariantWithNoFields`.
